# Performance budgets — `bracket-filled.fsm`, 1080p viewport

**Generated by** `web/tests/probe-budgets.mjs`, run `2026-10-07`.

The referee is the headed pass (GOAL.md names a real browser on a real display).
The headless pass records what CI sees; headless Chromium holds the main thread on
presented-frame back-pressure inside its GPU-process pipeline for ~100-250 ms after
an edit even though the app JS costs ~0.5 ms per frame — see the note below.

Headless caveat, measured: every headless run here (SwiftShader and ANGLE/Vulkan
on an RTX 5090) reports one 123-236 ms long task per edit; a trace ties it to a
single GPU-process `WebGL` command-buffer flush of 127-183 ms, with the renderer
main thread waiting inside one umbrella rAF task. Hiding the raymarch quad, hiding
overlays, forced GC and warm shader caches make no difference; the app JS costs
0.2-0.6 ms per frame. The headed run on the same machine records no long tasks and
a 59.9-60.0 fps presented cadence. The headless number is therefore a harness
artifact, and the headed pass is the budget referee.

Export budget (3MF of the graded bracket at 0.1 mm feature resolution, ≤ 15 s): the
"export 3MF at h 0.1" row measures it through the real Make UI in Chrome — mesh time
from the export meta, write time from the timed download click. The click→meta wall
also carries the export health report (field-volume reference and defect scan), which
the budget row does not include; both wall and report times are in the detail.
This run: the row passes in every pass above (headless, headed).
Defect classes and their classification: `docs/verification/V8.md`, section
"Adaptive dual contouring (the browser export path)".

Mesh-doc rows (M6): "mesh doc import" times the shipped 12-triangle GLB fixture
through the real file palette — chooser settle, weld, segment and the worker
voxelise, up to the mesh node landing in the document; "mesh doc export" runs the
same Make-lens 3MF measurement as the bracket row on that imported part. The
fixture is not budget-scale: the 87k-triangle Meshy STL the milestone names is
measured natively in `docs/verification/V10.md`.

Machine: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-Core Processor, 32 hardware threads, 249 GiB RAM, linux. Every timing above is this machine's; GOAL's mid-range laptop
is not measured here.
